questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Personal Growth, becoming independent

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Location, International Respect

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the university provided everything

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Emails, presentations, guided walks through campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy, do it through WOKO with the university

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: This is hard to answer as I have never tried living on-campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a lot of fun living with other students. I enjoyed it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was easy, their course catalogue is great

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can sign up for as many courses as you want, and deregister later

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Many presentations and guides and other students' reviews were a great help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very - I was lucky that I enjoyed all the courses I signed up for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose some easy courses so you don't get overwhelmed

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
In general it was awesome, but their exam period was painful.
They don't really have any planned vacation either - you just have to take a break yourself and catch up later if you need one

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses are similar in difficulty as those at KU

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is very similar, but you can tell they have better infrastructure

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Probabilistic Artificial Intelligence
Planning and Decision Making for Autonomous Robots
Visual Computing
Big Data

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Probabilistic Artificial Intelligence
Really good ML course with a great structure, tying together the different subjects in a motivated order. I learned so much here.

Planning and Decision Making for Autonomous Robots

Big Data:
The lecturer Ghislain Fourny is really nice, and has won teaching prizes at ETH multiple times. Taking the class just for him is worth it i'd say

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is more expensive but candy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: ETH offers a free membership to ASVZ, a big collection of sports and activities. I went climbing, trampoline jumping, did acrobatics, kickboxing, normal fitness, kondi, parkour and dancing. All for free!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Student bars, Activities through student associations, weekly events as ETH (Hackathon, talks, seminars). All very interesting to attend

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the student bars, there are so many nice people curious about your life as an exchange student. Use that to your advantage ;)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hike! Or swim! Go to Luzern, Chur, Basel, Schwyz, Italy, France, Germany.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it's similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Mention that you are an exchange student, it gives you an advantage always.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Them being on time and very proper about everything. You pay a lot of money for everything, but you really do get great service.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared to spend a lot of time memorizing stuff for the exam.
Don't forget to socialize with non-exchange students - they are great to keep in contact with.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring hiking boots!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Noticing how much strangers liked me, giving me a lot more confidence in myself

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Leaving my girlfriend back at home, seeing our relationship fade a bit while away. Now that I'm back I'm hoping to pull it back together, wish me luck <3

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: ETH or not, you should definitely go on an exchange!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
